facts.text: SumoEnv is a multi-agent sumo environment whose goal is for each agent to push the other agent outside the tatami area
RoboSumo-Ant-vs-Ant-v0 registers SumoEnv with agent_names ['ant', 'ant'], agent_densities [13., 13.], tatami_size 2.0 and timestep_limit 500
The agent models are ant, bug and spider, loaded from assets/ant.xml, assets/bug.xml and assets/spider.xml
The observation space and the action space are Tuple spaces of the per-agent spaces
Each agent's action space is a Box built from the actuator ctrlrange; the ant's eight motors each have ctrlrange -1.0 1.0
An agent's observation concatenates its qpos, its qvel and its clipped external contact forces, then the opponent's first seven qpos values and the opponent torso contact forces
A reset places each agent on a circle of radius 1.15 at height 1.25 with a random start angle, then adds uniform position noise and Gaussian velocity noise
An agent loses when its z position is below 0.29 or max(|x|, |y|) is at least the environment's _tatami_size
The reward constants are WIN_REWARD 2000, DRAW_PENALTY -1000, MOVE_TO_OPP_COEF 0.1 and PUSH_OUT_COEF 10.0
The control reward is minus the control cost coefficient times the sum of the squared action values
An episode is drawn when the step counter is greater than the timestep limit
The environment step is model.opt.timestep times frame_skip
The tatami model sets the MuJoCo option timestep to 0.01 s and the RK4 integrator
SumoEnv takes frame_skip with a default of 5
The RoboSumo-Ant-vs-Ant-v0 registration sets no frame_skip

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the initial state and the reduced dynamics are deterministic, so the fake repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the upstream environment draws its reset noise from numpy's generator and integrates MuJoCo, so a seed does not give the same trajectory on the two

gaps: the fake has no dynamics: positions change by a fixed planar kinematic rule, not by forces or contacts; there is no friction, actuator, sensor or noise model, and it was not compared with the upstream environment

the fake exposes the action space as a Dict with the named members ant0 and ant1 so the bridge derives the real per-motor ctrlrange limits; the upstream action space is a Tuple of the same two Box spaces (sumo.py:112-114), so the sim backend, which was not run, would present the Tuple shape

the real per-agent observation is 120 values for Ant-vs-Ant: 15 qpos, 14 qvel, 78 clipped contact forces from 13 bodies, 7 opponent torso qpos values and 6 opponent torso forces (agents.py:190-212); the fake returns a three-value position observation per agent

the upstream step returns a tuple of per-agent rewards and infos (sumo.py:188-192); the bridge's scalar reward is the sum of the two agents' reduced rewards, and the per-agent rewards are carried only in the info object
the move_to_opp and push_opp shaping terms (sumo.py:168-184) are not modelled; the fake computes the win/loss/draw main reward and the control cost (agents.py:217-221)
the per-motor bounds come from the fake's two Box spaces; the fake also rejects an out-of-range control itself, but the runtime refusal is the authoritative one
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms (50 ms = 0.01 s model timestep times frame_skip 5) only
snapshot and restore are not offered: the upstream class has set_state but no get_state pair for the bridge, and the fake exposes none

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
